title: CURVE: Learning Causality-Inspired Invariant Representations for Robust Scene Understanding via Uncertainty-Guided Regularization
claim: Existing latent and dense-graph approaches pick up spurious environment correlations and fail out of distribution; ours adjusts causally and sparsifies the graph.
layout: 3 panels: two prior-work boxes on top, our method below, arrows pointing down
description: The figure has three rounded panels. The top-left panel, "Latent Representation–Based Scene Understanding", shows two driving photos (an input and an out-of-distribution one). The input goes through deep learning encoders into a black-box embedding drawn as a tangled box with a big orange question mark. Dashed arrows lead to icons for poor adaptation (a jagged line chart with a warning sign) and limited interpretability (a brain with a magnifier and a red X). The top-right panel, "Existing Scene Graph Representation", shows a dense graph of blue and orange object icons (car, pedestrian, tree, traffic light) with many criss-crossing edges. It also shows the failure of disentanglement, with an inequality in math. Orange arrows labeled "Out-of-Distribution Failure" point down to the bottom orange panel, "Causal Uncertainty-aware Representation". There, environment prototypes (weather icons) feed a causal adjustment, which combines with high-uncertainty pruning by scissors to give a sparse graph. Blue and orange are the main colors.
caption: CURVE mitigates OOD failures by counteracting environment-driven dense edges. The top panels illustrate OOD failures in latent/dense graph approaches, as dense connectivity induces environment-conditioned edges, encouraging shortcut reliance on background co-occurrences. The bottom panel demonstrates our method using soft causal backdoor adjustment and uncertainty-driven sparsification to separate factors and produce a sparse, robust graph.
abstract: Scene graphs provide structured abstractions for scene understanding, yet they often overfit to spurious correlations, severely hindering out-of-distribution generalization. To address this limitation, we propose CURVE, a causality-inspired framework that integrates variational uncertainty modeling with uncertainty-guided structural regularization to suppress high-variance, environment-specific relations. Specifically, we apply prototype-conditioned debiasing to disentangle invariant interaction dynamics from environment-dependent variations, promoting a sparse and domain-stable topology. Empirically, we evaluate CURVE in zero-shot transfer and low-data sim-to-real adaptation, verifying its ability to learn domain-stable sparse topologies and provide reliable uncertainty estimates to support risk prediction under distribution shifts.
